podcast.title: 1986 Alt-Rock Radio Playlists
podcast.body: Steve Winwood's songs were part of alt-rock radio playlists in late 1986, highlighting the wide array of artists and genres, including those less typically associated with "alternative," that were played at the time. "If you go through the radio playlists for, say, late 1986, you'll find Peter Gabriel, the Smiths, R.E.M., New Order, Depeche Mode, Paul Simon's Graceland album, The Cure, Steve Winwood."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Michelob Beer Commercial (1988)
podcast.body: Steve Winwood, a solo superstar and former Traffic frontman, featured in a Michelob Beer ad campaign with a "totally new song" titled "What the Night Can Do." This followed Eric Clapton's appearance for the same brand and contributed to the song's chart success. "Mikalo dropped an ad featuring a totally new song by former traffic frontman, now solo superstar Steve Winnwood."

podcast.title: Disputed Song Origin
podcast.body: The media expressed skepticism and "didn't believe" Steve Winwood's claim that his song "What the Night Can Do" was written prior to striking the Michelob deal. The song's sound was so strongly associated with a beer commercial that its independent artistic origin was questioned, reflecting ongoing debates about music authenticity. "Sounded so much like a beer commercial that the media didn't believe Winnwood when he claimed the song was written before the Mikalobe deal was struck."
